BPAYBS.description: Back pay owed for an earlier period under a contract version signed later, at the amount entered or computed by the run. Wages for EPF, SOCSO, EIS and HRD; PCB taxes it as additional remuneration in the month paid.

ADJ.description: A salary adjustment for an earlier period, paid at the amount entered. It counts as wages for EPF and the HRD levy, as back pay does.

references.title: EPF Act 1991 (Act 452) s.2 "wages" includes any bonus (AGC text as at 1 July 2022); PCB additional remuneration (LHDN MTD Specification 2026 D(b)(2)). Excluded from SOCSO, EIS and SKBBK wages by Act 4 s.2(24)(e) "bonus tahunan" (PERKESO BM reprint as at 1 July 2021, p.18) and Act 800 s.2 "wages" (e) "any annual bonus", and from HRD wages by Act 612 s.2 "wages" (e) "any bonus or commission" (AGC reprint 2017).

BONUS.description: A bonus at the amount entered. EPF wages; not SOCSO, EIS or SKBBK wages (Act 4 s.2(24)(e)) or HRD wages; PCB taxes it as additional remuneration in the month paid.

references.title: ITA 1967 Schedule 6 para 25C (AGC online text as at 1 January 2026): a long service award is exempt up to RM2,000 per year of assessment after more than ten years with the same employer; the rest is additional remuneration for MTD (LHDN MTD Specification 2026 D(b)(2), E(9) item v) — PCB subtracts the exempt part. EPF Act 1991 s.2 "wages" (AGC text as at 1 July 2022) excludes (c) "any gratuity", unqualified, and KWSP's employer FAQ (Mandatory Contribution, Q11 "Non-Wages", read 28 September 2026) lists "Gratuity" among payments not liable. law silent on whether a long service award is a gratuity; default — it is (a payment in recognition of length of service, not remuneration for work done), so outside EPF; lawful because s.2 excludes every gratuity and s.43 charges only "wages". Act 4 s.2(24)(d) (PERKESO BM reprint as at 1 July 2021) and Act 800 s.2 "wages" (d) exclude only a gratuity "payable on discharge or retirement", and (e) only an annual bonus, so an award paid in service is SOCSO, EIS and (A1788, from 1 June 2026) SKBBK wages. Act 612 s.2 "wages" (AGC reprint 2017) is basic salary, fixed allowances, leave pay and arrears: a one-off award is none of them, so outside the HRD levy. A past-achievement, service-excellence, innovation or productivity award (the rest of para 25C) is not this class.

LONG_SERVICE_AWARD.description: A long-service award, at the amount entered. It is tax-exempt up to RM2,000 a year after more than ten years with the employer (Income Tax Act 1967 Schedule 6 para 25C).

references.title: ITA 1967 Schedule 6 para 25C (AGC online text as at 1 January 2026): a perquisite consisting of a past achievement, service excellence, innovation or productivity award, whether in money or otherwise, is exempt up to RM2,000 per employee per year of assessment — one cap shared with the long service award (which counts only after more than ten years with the same employer); LHDN Public Ruling 5/2019 Perquisites from Employment (https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/PR_05_2019_2.pdf) para 7.1.1 and Example 11 (p.18): the RM2,000 covers the awards together. LHDN Specification for MTD Calculations Using Computerised Calculation 2026 (https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-2026.pdf), E(9), pp.20–22, read 28 September 2026 item v: the exempt part is excluded from MTD remuneration and the rest is additional remuneration (D(b)(2) “bonus/incentive”); PCB subtracts the shared exemption. EPF Act 1991 s.2 “wages” (AGC text as at 1 July 2022) includes any bonus, commission or allowance and excludes any travelling allowance; KWSP employer FAQ (Mandatory Contribution, Q8 “Components of Wage”: salary, bonus, allowance, commission, incentives; Q11 “Non-Wages”: travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession; read 28 September 2026): an award is a bonus or incentive, so EPF wages (additional). Act 4 s.2(24) (PERKESO BM reprint as at 1 July 2021) and Act 800 s.2 “wages” exclude (b) any travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession, (c) sums to defray special expenses entailed by the nature of the employment, (d) a gratuity on discharge or retirement and (e) an annual bonus: an in-service award is none of these, so SOCSO, EIS and (A1788, from 1 June 2026) SKBBK wages. Act 612 s.2 “wages” (AGC reprint 2017): basic salary and fixed allowances or other emoluments of a like nature paid in cash, excluding (b) any travelling allowance, (c) special expenses and (e) any bonus or commission: an award is no fixed allowance and is a bonus, so outside the HRD levy. A long service award is its own class, LONG_SERVICE_AWARD.

EXCELLENCE_AWARD.description: An award for past achievement, service excellence, innovation or productivity, at the amount entered. It is tax-exempt up to RM2,000 a year (Income Tax Act 1967 Schedule 6 para 25C).

references.title: LHDN Specification for MTD Calculations Using Computerised Calculation 2026 (https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-2026.pdf), E(9), pp.20–22, read 28 September 2026 item i: petrol card, petrol allowance, travelling allowance or toll payment, or any combination, for official duties is exempt up to RM6,000 a year; LHDN Public Ruling 5/2019 Perquisites from Employment (https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/PR_05_2019_2.pdf) para 7.2.1 (pp.20–21, Example 17: RM7,200 + RM3,600 → RM6,000 exempt, RM4,800 taxable). PCB subtracts the year's first RM6,000; the rest is normal remuneration (spec D(1)). EPF Act 1991 s.2 “wages” (AGC text as at 1 July 2022) includes any bonus, commission or allowance and excludes any travelling allowance; KWSP employer FAQ (Mandatory Contribution, Q8 “Components of Wage”: salary, bonus, allowance, commission, incentives; Q11 “Non-Wages”: travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession; read 28 September 2026); Act 4 s.2(24) (PERKESO BM reprint as at 1 July 2021) and Act 800 s.2 “wages” exclude (b) any travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession, (c) sums to defray special expenses entailed by the nature of the employment, (d) a gratuity on discharge or retirement and (e) an annual bonus; Act 612 s.2 “wages” (AGC reprint 2017): basic salary and fixed allowances or other emoluments of a like nature paid in cash, excluding (b) any travelling allowance, (c) special expenses and (e) any bonus or commission; Employment Act 1955 s.2 “wages” (AGC reprint as at 1 August 2023): basic wages and all other payments in cash payable for work done under the contract, excluding (c) any travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession: so this class enters no contribution base, no First Schedule wage and no ordinary rate of pay. An ad hoc class, not a contract allowance, because `terms.monthly_wage` (the s.60I ordinary rate) sums every contract allowance. Travel between home and work is not this class.

TRAVEL_OFFICIAL.description: Pays petrol, toll or travelling costs for official duties, at the amount entered. The first RM6,000 a year is tax-exempt (LHDN MTD specification 2026 E(9)).

references.title: Employment (Termination and Lay-Off Benefits) Regulations 1980 reg.6(1): an employee of twelve months’ continuous service whose contract is terminated other than for misconduct, retirement or resignation is paid ten days’ wages for every year of service under two years, fifteen under five and twenty at five or more, pro rata for a part year; reg.4(1)(b) excludes misconduct dismissal after due inquiry. EA 1955 First Schedule paras 1A, 2(1)-(4) and 3: the s.60J wage exclusion does not apply to qualifying manual workers, manual-labour supervisors, commercial vehicle operators or vessel workers, irrespective of wages. The vessel category is excluded from Part XII, not Part XIIA. Domestic employees are excluded from Part XIIA by para.2(5). The statutory work category must represent the applicable First Schedule profile. The separate reg.1A part-time and reg.7 outworker exclusions still require their own classification; this wage-category correction does not close those mechanisms. reg.6(2): a day's wages uses the actual s.2 wages of the twelve completed months immediately preceding termination, divided by365 under JTKSM's published formula. The exact original native payroll and documented same-employer prior_payroll records establish the amount and dates; no entered average, contractual-salary fallback or partial-history extrapolation is used. reg.4(1): payable on termination "for any reason whatsoever" other than contractual retirement, misconduct after due inquiry or voluntary resignation — a RETRENCHMENT or UNILATERAL termination is inside it. reg.8: none is payable where the employee's service is transferred to and continued by the new employer on terms no less favourable, the service counting with that employer — TRANSFER and TRANSFER_TO_SUBSIDIARY are excluded. Employment (Termination and Lay-Off Benefits) Regulations 1980 (https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/sites/default/files/2023-03/8.%20EMPLOYMENT%20(TERMINATION%20&%20LAY%20OFF%20BENEFITS)%20REGULATIONS%201980_0.pdf) regs 3–4 and 6: not less than 10 / 15 / 20 days' wages for every year of continuous service (under two, two to under five, five or more years), pro rata to the nearest month, a day's wages being the average true day's wages over the twelve completed months before (the exact original twelve-month statutory wage total divided by365; genuine external sources retain their documented dates and signed component amounts), the entered amount if higher; not on contractual retirement, a misconduct dismissal after inquiry or a resignation other than under s.13(2) / s.14(3); First Schedule para 1A takes s.60J from a non-manual employee above RM4,000. Taxable compensation for loss of employment above RM10,000 a completed year of service (ITA Sch.6 para 15(1)(b), https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/3345910_BI/Act%2053%20(Online%202026).pdf; the RM20,000 rate applied only to exits in 2020–2021) — additional remuneration in PCB, less the exemption.

TERMINATION_BENEFIT.description: Termination benefit for an employee with at least twelve months' service whose contract ends other than by misconduct, retirement or resignation: 10, 15 or 20 days' wages for each year of service (under two years, two to under five, five or more), a part year pro rata to the nearest month. The computed floor is the contract's monthly wage with its fixed allowances × 12 ÷ 365 per day; enter the amount from the actual twelve months' wages where it is higher (Employment (Termination and Lay-Off Benefits) Regulations 1980 reg.6).

references.title: Employment Act 1955 ss.12(2)-(4),13(1),14(1)(a),57. A written contractual notice governs; absent it, general default notice is 4/6/8 weeks at under 2/under 5/at least 5 years on the notice-giving date. Section 12(3) preserves that statutory floor for redundancy/retrenchment. Domestic employment has a separate 14-day default, subject to its express contract. Written notice includes its giving day. Section 13(1) indemnifies only wages that would accrue during the unexpired notice; days already served and expressly waived final days are removed. Dismissal for misconduct after due inquiry owes no notice under s.14(1)(a). constant monthly wages are apportioned over the actual unserved calendar interval by each month's length, replacing monthly/30. This row does not yet resolve every wage component, changing/non-monthly wage or contractual calendar-month notice; those R14 branches remain open. Source: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf the actual terminating party controls payment direction. Sections 13(2),14(3),57 supply distinct exception  Section 14 does not apply to domestic employees (First Schedule para.2(5)); s.17A requires both approved form and filed copy, not an INTERN label. Section 12(3) floor also reads the specified structural/transfer/ownership ground. Approved apprenticeship contractual rights remain separately unresolved. EA ss.12–13: the indemnity is the wages that would have accrued over the notice, or its unexpired part — the written contract's notice (terms.contract_notice_weeks), else not less than 4 / 6 / 8 weeks by service, the floor also applying on the s.12(3) structural grounds — less the days served from notice_given_on and the waived days; the wages of a day are terms.monthly_wage × 12 ÷ 365. The entered amount if higher.

NOTICE_IN_LIEU.description: Indemnity paid instead of notice under Employment Act 1955 s.13(1), at the amount entered. Not wages for EPF, SOCSO or EIS; taxable.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 ss.13(1),24(2)(b): indemnity owed by the party ending employment to the other party. A supported manual request retains required evidence and review; its entered amount does not override the calculated unserved-period wages. Employee recovery remains NET/SUBTRACT, subject to the applicable deduction limits and the separate final-wages exception in s.24(9)(b). Section 24(9)(a) concerns compensation paid BY the employer, not this employee debt. Statutory exceptions, the approved-and-filed apprenticeship exclusion and domestic scope are evaluated from declared  Constant-monthly valuation and outstanding wage/contract branches share NOTICE_IN_LIEU.

NOTICE_INDEMNITY.description: Recovers from the employee's pay the indemnity owed for notice not served, at the amount entered (Employment Act 1955 s.13(1)).

TASK_MONTHLY_WAGE.description: The month's wage of an employee paid by the task (statutory_work_category TASK_BASIS), at the amount entered. Ordinary wages.

COMMISSION_MONTHLY.description: A commission paid every month, at the amount entered, for an employee paid by the task or by the piece. It is part of the month's wages for EPF, SOCSO, EIS and PCB.

references.title: Minimum Wages Order 2024 para 5(2); EPF Act 1991 s.43; PERKESO wage guidance; LHDN 2026 MTD specification s.D; HRD Corp levy guideline

COMMISSION_IRREGULAR.description: A commission that is not paid every month, at the amount entered, for an employee paid by the task or by the piece. It is wages for EPF, SOCSO and EIS, and PCB taxes it in the month it is paid.

references.title: Workers’ Minimum Standards of Housing and Amenities Act 1990 (Act 446), P.U.(A)249/2020 para 2; JTKSM accommodation FAQ (https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/ms/soalan-lazim/perumahan-penginapan-dan-kemudahan-pekerja): maximum RM100 per worker per month. A JTKSM accommodation certificate currently in force is required, including centralised accommodation. The contractual charge remains binding: an increase, including a change from free accommodation, requires prior written agreement. Estate housing cannot be charged. Rent is a net deduction and does not reduce contributable wages. The event date records the rent liability date in the evidenced rent month; each month’s requests share the lower contractual/statutory ceiling. A written variation is recognised only from its recorded agreement date. EA s.24(4)(e)–(5) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf): a deduction for accommodation, services, food or meals only at the employee's written request (entry fact written_request) with the Director General's prior permission. The cap comes from the Workers' Minimum Standards of Housing, Accommodations and Amenities Act 1990 (Act 446) and its regulations, not s.24.

ACCOMMODATION_RENT.description: Deducts the month's rent for employer-provided accommodation from net pay: the amount entered, and no more than RM100 a month (Workers' Minimum Standards of Housing and Amenities Act 1990).

references.title: Income Tax Act 1967 s.107 direction (Form CP38): LHDN directs the employer to deduct a fixed instalment of the employee's own tax and remit it with the month's MTD (PCB_REMITTANCE). It is not MTD: it never enters the accumulated MTD X (MTD Specification 2026 D, X "shall not include … payment of tax installment", https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-2026.pdf) and is not an EA s.24(8) exception. Customer input: the directed amount per month.

CP38_INSTALMENT.description: Deducts from net pay the tax instalment LHDN directs on Form CP38, at the amount entered. It is the employee's tax, remitted with the monthly tax deduction (PCB) and counted in the tax the payslip withholds, but kept out of the accumulated PCB the next month's PCB is worked out from (Income Tax Act 1967 s.107).

references.title: Employment (Termination and Lay-Off Benefits) Regulations 1980 (https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/sites/default/files/2023-03/8.%20EMPLOYMENT%20(TERMINATION%20&%20LAY%20OFF%20BENEFITS)%20REGULATIONS%201980_0.pdf) regs 3(1)(b), 5 and 6: an employee whose pay depends on being given work, not given it on at least twelve normal working days in four consecutive weeks (rest days, holidays and leave not counted), is paid the reg.6 benefit; not EPF, SOCSO or EIS wages (lay-off benefits are excluded from each Act's wages). The entered amount if higher; the lay-off itself is the employer's record. A day's wages (reg.6(2), "average true day's wages … over the period of twelve completed months' service"): the twelve months' wages ÷ 365, JTKSM's published formula (https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/en/frequently-asked-questions/employees-retrenchment/how-termination-benefit-payment-calculated-and, read 2026-10-07) — earned.months gross ÷ months × 12 ÷ 365, terms.monthly_wage × 12 ÷ 365 without history.

LAYOFF_BENEFIT.description: Lay-off benefit for an employee with at least twelve months' service who is given no work on twelve normal working days in four consecutive weeks: 10, 15 or 20 days' wages for each year of service (under two years, two to under five, five or more), a part year pro rata to the nearest month. The computed floor is the contract's monthly wage with its fixed allowances × 12 ÷ 365 per day; enter the amount from the actual twelve months' wages where it is higher (Employment (Termination and Lay-Off Benefits) Regulations 1980 reg.6).

PAYEE_PAYMENT.description: A payment to an agent, dealer or distributor engaged as a payee, at the amount entered. It is not employment income: no EPF, SOCSO, EIS, HRD levy or PCB (Income Tax Act 1967 s.83A(4)).

ZAKAT.description: Deducts zakat from pay at the amount entered, with the employee's written authorisation. It is shown on the payslip and reduces the year's tax in PCB.

references.title: Overtime on a normal working day at not less than 1.5 × the hourly rate (EA s.60A(3)(a)); at most 104 hours in a month (Employment (Limitation of Overtime Work) Regulations 1980 reg.2). Rest-day and public-holiday overtime are their own lines. EA s.60I(1A) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf): the ordinary rate of pay of a monthly-rated employee is the monthly rate ÷ 26; the hourly rate is that ÷ the normal hours of work (s.60I(1)(b), company.normal_daily_hours, 8 unrecorded). EA First Schedule paras 1A–2 (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf): these premia bind an employee earning not more than RM4,000 a month (s.2 wages less commission, subsistence and overtime: terms.monthly_wage) or engaged in manual labour, supervising it, operating or maintaining a commercial vehicle, or as vessel crew, whatever the pay; not a domestic employee (para 2(5)); terms.overtime_by_contract applies them by contract. EA s.60I (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf): the ordinary rate of pay is monthly ÷ 26 (s.60I(1A)), weekly ÷ 6 (s.60I(1B)), and for a daily, hourly or piece rate the preceding wage period's wages ÷ the days worked (s.60I(1C), the days of a piece or hourly worker read from the period's WORK-day hours ÷ the normal hours); the hourly rate is it ÷ the contract's normal hours a day (s.60I(1)(b), s.60A(3)(c); terms.normal_hours_per_day, else company.normal_daily_hours, else 8). Pay basis: terms.pay_basis. Part-time terms (Part-Time Employees Regulations 2010 regs 2, 4, 5, 6(6), 9(3), https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/sites/default/files/2023-03/10.%20Employment%20-%20Part-time%20Employees%20-%20Regulations%202010%20%20%281%29.pdf): the hours beyond the part-timer's normal hours up to a full-timer's day (company.normal_daily_hours, 8 by reg.4(1)) at 1.0× and beyond it at 1.5× the hourly rate. Fixed contractual cash allowances enter the ordinary monthly or weekly wage; travel or special-expense reimbursements belong in claims. Meal allowances receive no holiday uplift (EA s.60D(3)(b)).

OVERTIME.description: Overtime beyond normal hours on a working day, and every hour on an off day: 1.5 × the hourly ordinary rate of pay (Employment Act 1955 s.60A(3)(a)). A part-timer is paid 1 × up to a comparable full-timer's day, then 1.5 ×. For employees earning up to RM4,000 a month or in a First Schedule manual category.

references.title: Work on a rest day by a monthly-rated employee within the normal hours: half a day's wages for up to half the normal hours, one day's wages for more (EA s.60(3)(a)–(b), https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf). EA s.60I(1A): the ordinary rate of pay of a monthly-rated employee is the monthly rate ÷ 26; the hourly rate is that ÷ the normal hours of work (s.60I(1)(b), company.normal_daily_hours, 8 unrecorded). a daily, hourly or similar rate is paid one day's wages for up to half the normal hours and two days' for more (s.60(3)(a)); a monthly or weekly rate half a day's and a day's (s.60(3)(b)). EA First Schedule paras 1A–2: these premia bind an employee earning not more than RM4,000 a month (s.2 wages less commission, subsistence and overtime: terms.monthly_wage) or engaged in manual labour, supervising it, operating or maintaining a commercial vehicle, or as vessel crew, whatever the pay; not a domestic employee (para 2(5)); terms.overtime_by_contract applies them by contract. Fixed contractual cash allowances enter the ordinary monthly or weekly wage; travel or special-expense reimbursements belong in claims. Meal allowances receive no holiday uplift (EA s.60D(3)(b)).

REST_DAY_WORK.description: Work within normal hours on a rest day. Monthly-rated: half a day's wages for up to half the normal hours, one day's wages for more. Daily or hourly-rated: one day's wages, or two (Employment Act 1955 s.60(3)(a)-(b)). An employer rest-day hourly multiple applies where it pays more.

PCB subtracts the year's first RM3,000; the rest is normal remuneration. EPF Act 1991 s.2 “wages” (AGC text as at 1 July 2022) includes any bonus, commission or allowance and excludes any travelling allowance; KWSP employer FAQ (Mandatory Contribution, Q8 “Components of Wage”: salary, bonus, allowance, commission, incentives; Q11 “Non-Wages”: travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession; read 28 September 2026): an allowance is EPF wages. Act 4 s.2(24) and Act 800 s.2 include any allowance paid in money and exclude none of this kind: SOCSO, EIS and SKBBK wages. The RM3,000 limit has applied since YA2024 (Income Tax (Exemption) (Amendment) Order 2023, P.U.(A) 399/2023, raising the RM2,400), so every version from December 2025 carries it. Sub-monthly settlement: a fixed allowance is monthly wages under EA s.18A — the whole month ÷ the parts, a part month the employed days ÷ the month's calendar days, the last part settling the month less what the earlier parts paid.

references.locator: s.43 and Third Schedule Parts A and E
references.quote: Part A: Malaysian citizens, permanent residents and pre-1-August-1998 electors below 60; Part E: Malaysian citizens aged 60 and above (Part E by its own terms reaches Malaysian citizens only). A non-citizen contributes under Part F; a permanent resident or pre-1998 elector aged 60 or above contributes under Part C. The first printed row of both Parts is NIL: wages of RM0.01 to RM10.00 attract no contribution. Above the table the total contribution is rounded up to the next ringgit and the employer’s share is that total less the employee’s rounded share, never two separate round-ups. Bands: RM20 to RM5,000, RM100 to RM20,000, contribution taken on the band's upper limit; employee 11%, employer 13% up to RM5,000 and 12% above; above RM20,000 each share is its percentage of the wage; Part E is the employer's 4% alone. Part A note under the RM5,000 row: "Where the employer pays bonus to an employee who receives monthly wages of RM5,000.00 and below, and upon receiving the said bonus renders the wages received for that month to exceed RM5,000.00, the employer’s contribution shall be calculated at the rate of 13% of the amount of wages for the month. The total contribution which includes cents shall be rounded to the next ringgit." The employee's share stays on the printed row. The Act does not state how the total splits between the two shares above RM20,000. Part A para 1(c) and Part C para 1(c): a non-citizen who elected to contribute before 1 August 1998 stays on Part A below 60 and Part C from 60. The same bonus note covers those electors.

A domestic servant is not an employee unless the employee gave one month's notice to be a member (paras (2)-(3)). A student on industrial training engaged without a contract of service or apprenticeship is not an employee (s.2).

MINIMUM_WAGE_MONTHLY.description: Checks that a monthly-rated employee's agreed salary is at least the RM1,700 monthly minimum wage.

references.title: Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 2, 3(1), 5(1)
references.locator: RM1,700 a month for a monthly-rated employee; para 2 leaves out only a domestic employee as EA s.2(1) defines one. An apprentice is inside: the National Wages Consultative Council (Amendment) Act 2025 brought apprenticeship contracts into Act 732 from 1 August 2025.

MINIMUM_WAGE_HOURLY_PART_TIME.description: Checks that a part-time employee's agreed rate, converted to an hourly equivalent, meets the RM8.72 hourly minimum.

references.title: Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1), 5(1)
references.locator: RM8.72 an hour, including a part-time employee's rate derived from the agreed month, week or day.

references.title: Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations 2010 [P.U.(A) 302/2010]
references.locator: the part-time hourly rate is the agreed rate divided by the agreed normal hours.

LABOUR_ORDINANCE_TERRITORY.description: Rejects a Sabah or Sarawak worksite, which is governed by its own Labour Ordinance rather than the Employment Act.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) First Schedule
references.locator: the Act governs Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan.

references.title: Labour Ordinance (Sabah) Cap. 67; Labour Ordinance (Sarawak) Cap. 76
references.locator: a Sabah or Sarawak worksite is governed by its own Ordinance, which this lineage does not encode.

NORMAL_HOURS_WEEK.description: Checks that agreed normal weekly hours do not exceed 45, except for shift work averaged over three weeks.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(d)
references.locator: the normal hours of work may not exceed 45 in one week.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60C(1)
references.locator: shift work may average the normal hours over three weeks.

MINIMUM_WAGE_DAILY.description: Checks that a daily-rated employee's agreed rate meets the daily minimum wage for a four-, five- or six-day week.

references.title: Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1), 5(1)
references.locator: RM98.08, RM78.46 and RM65.38 a day for a four-, five- and six-day week.

MINIMUM_WAGE_HOURLY.description: Checks that an hourly-rated employee's agreed rate is at least RM8.72 an hour.

WAGE_PAYMENT_METHOD.description: Requires wages to be paid into the employee's bank account unless a non-bank method has the Director General's approval.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265)
references.quote: Wages are paid through a bank account opened in the employee's name unless the employee makes a written request for another method; payment in cash or by cheque needs the Director General's approval.

WAGE_PERIOD.description: Checks that the employer's payment schedule does not cover more than one month.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.18
references.locator: a wage period may not exceed one month.

ROSTER_CONTINUOUS_HOURS.description: Requires a thirty-minute break in planned overtime that would run more than five consecutive hours, judged on the breaks each span records.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(a) and proviso (i)
references.locator: no more than five consecutive hours without a period of leisure of not less than thirty minutes; a break of less than thirty minutes does not break the continuity of the five hours.

ROSTER_DAILY_TOTAL.description: Checks that the rostered shift and its planned overtime do not take a day beyond twelve hours of work, and that a month's overtime on working or off days stays within the statutory cap; rest-day work is outside that cap.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(7) and s.60C(2)
references.locator: except in the emergencies of s.60A(2)(a) to (e), no employer shall require any employee to work for more than twelve hours in any one day, overtime and rest-day work included.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(9)
references.locator: hours of work: the time the employee is at the disposal of the employer; an unpaid break is not.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(4)(a); Employment (Limitation of Overtime Work) Regulations 1980 reg.2
references.locator: overtime is limited to one hundred and four hours in any one month. The proviso in s.60A(4)(a) leaves work on a rest day or a gazetted public holiday out of the cap, though it is still paid at the rest-day and holiday rates. Off days are not that statutory rest day, so their hours count.

CHILD_EMPLOYMENT.description: Requires a permitted employment category for a worker under fifteen.

references.title: Children and Young Persons (Employment) Act 1966 (Act 350) s.2(2)
references.locator: a child under fifteen may work only in light family work, licensed public entertainment, school-approved work or an approved apprenticeship.

CHILD_LIGHT_WORK_AGE.description: Requires a worker doing light family work to be at least thirteen.

references.title: Children and Young Persons (Employment) Act 1966 (Act 350) s.2(2A)
references.locator: light work in a family undertaking requires age thirteen or above.

MINOR_HAZARDOUS_WORK.description: Prohibits hazardous work for a child and requires personal supervision and training for a young person.

references.title: Children and Young Persons (Employment) Act 1966 (Act 350) s.2(1A)–(1B), Fourth Schedule
references.locator: hazardous work is prohibited for a child; a young person needs personal supervision and an apprenticeship or vocational training.

MINOR_PROHIBITED_EMPLOYMENT.description: Prohibits Fifth Schedule employment for anyone under eighteen.

references.title: Children and Young Persons (Employment) Act 1966 (Act 350) s.2(2B), Fifth Schedule
references.locator: Fifth Schedule employment is prohibited for every person under eighteen; training does not exempt it.

CONTRACT_CATEGORIES.description: Restricts the contract's statutory work category and residency status to the values this jurisdiction recognises.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule (as amended by Act A1651, 1 January 2023)
references.locator: the statutory work category fixes coverage and the overtime, rest-day and holiday premia.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.2(1) "domestic employee"; EPF Act 1991 First Schedule para (2)
references.quote: Work of a private dwelling-house, not of a trade, business or profession carried on by the employer. EPF para (2) keeps a domestic servant of a registered business, society or corporation in the Fund: such a person is not this category.

SHARED_STRUCTURED_EMPLOYEE_INPUTS.description: Checks the annual-leave carry limit against the jurisdiction's minimum.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule
references.locator: the recorded worksite region must be one this lineage governs.

references.title: Agreed annual-leave carry
references.locator: the contract may not agree a negative carry limit.

HRD_LIABILITY_EVENT_DATE_REQUIRED.description: Requires a sealed employer that is HRD-compulsory or not registered to record the date its registration liability began.

references.title: Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Berhad Act 2001 (Act 612) s.4 and First Schedule
references.locator: a compulsory employer's registration liability runs from the actual date it began.

BUSINESS_CASE_SUBJECT_AND_REFERENCE.description: Requires a death, departure or non-bank wage case to name the employment and carry its source document.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.25A
references.locator: a non-bank wage request is the employee's signed writing, not an employer note.

references.title: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53) s.83(4)
references.locator: a departure from Malaysia needs the actual expected departure and its CP21 review.

BUSINESS_CASE_SIGNED_CONSENT.description: Requires a non-bank wage request to carry the employee's signed request, dated on or before the case was opened.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.25A(1)
references.locator: cash or cheque payment needs the employee's written request, signed before it takes effect.

DEPARTURE_CASE_ACTUAL_SCHEDULE.description: Requires an overseas departure case to record the actual expected departure date and any later return date.

references.title: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53) s.83(4)–(5)
references.locator: the employer gives CP21 notice before the actual departure; a known ordered return date cannot precede it.

DEATH_NOTICE_ACTUAL_RECEIPT.description: Checks that the employer's recorded notice of death does not precede the death.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.19–21
references.locator: the employer's notice of the employee's death starts the final-wage duty; it cannot precede the recorded death.

ANNUAL_LEAVE_SERVICE.description: Applies the annual-leave service rules for unauthorised absence and more than thirty days of unpaid leave in a year.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) s.60E(1), second proviso
references.locator: absence without permission and without reasonable excuse on more than ten per cent of the working days of the twelve months: no such leave.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) s.60E(3B)
references.locator: leave of absence without pay exceeding thirty days in the aggregate in any twelve months is disregarded in computing the length of service.

ANNUAL_LEAVE_SERVICE.condition:
if (get(ctx.entry, 'encashment', false) === true) return false;
return get(first(ctx.reads.leave_catalog), 'code', '') === 'ANNUAL_LEAVE';

PATERNITY_QUALIFYING_SERVICE.description: Requires twelve months' continuous service before paternity leave begins.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 (Act 265) s.60FA(3)(a)
references.locator: employed by the same employer at least twelve months immediately before the commencement of the paternity leave.

entity_extension_schema.title: MY entity extension data
entity_extension_schema.description: Additional employer compliance data on the sealed employer version, stored as entity_extension_data; the CEL root `employer.entity_extension_data`.

hrd_scope.title: HRD employer scope
hrd_scope.description: Part I industry, listed Part II NGO activity, or excluded employer under the effective First Schedule.

hrd_registration_class.title: HRD employer registration class
hrd_registration_class.description: Employer-level HRD Corp standing, retained after a headcount fall until approved deregistration.

hrd_education_schedule_code.title: 2026 HRD education exemption schedule code
hrd_education_schedule_code.description: P.U. (A) 13/2026 Schedule MSIC code or listed 8541/8542/8549 group; NONE when the registered education industry is not scheduled. Verify against the employer's HRD registration.

pdpa_dpo_required.title: Data protection officer required (PDPA s.12A)
pdpa_dpo_required.description: True where the entity processes personal data of more than 20,000 data subjects, sensitive personal data including financial information of more than 10,000, or carries on regular and systematic monitoring (Commissioner's DPO Guideline para 4.2, under Personal Data Protection Act 2010 s.12A).

hrd_registration_liability_on.title: HRD compulsory registration liability began on
hrd_registration_liability_on.description: The actual date this employer first met the applicable compulsory PSMB coverage conditions, supported by the real workforce/sector history or an authority determination. This is not incorporation or first employment by default.

ceased_on.title: Cessation date
ceased_on.description: The day the employer ceased operations for this registration.

employee_extension_schema.title: MY employee extension data

controls_employer.title: Controls the employer (no perquisite exemptions)
controls_employer.description: LHDN PR 5/2019 para 7.5 and MTD Specification 2026 E(9): the exempt allowances and awards do not apply to an employee with control over the employer.

paternity_confinements.title: Verified paternity confinement history
paternity_confinements.description: One record per confinement, including earlier employers/spouses. Set event_id to the date of its CHILD_BIRTH event. Record the actual lifetime ordinal and whether the s60FA notification requirement was met: at least thirty days before the expected confinement, or as early as possible after the birth.

overtime_by_contract.title: Statutory premia by contract
overtime_by_contract.description: First Schedule para 1A takes ss.60(3), 60A(3), 60D(3) from a non-manual employee above RM4,000; true where the contract grants them anyway.

shift_work.title: Shift work
shift_work.description: EA s.60C: normal hours averaged over three weeks.

industrial_training_student.title: Industrial-training student without a contract of service
industrial_training_student.description: EPF Act 1991 s.2, Employees’ Social Security Act 1969 s.2(5) and Employment Insurance System Act 2017 s.2: a person not employed under a contract of service or apprenticeship is not an employee — no EPF, SOCSO, SKBBK or EIS. Reported as status 5 (Pelatih Industri) in the C.P.8D.

contractual_epf_employer_rate.title: Contractual employer EPF rate (above the Third Schedule)

minor_employment_kind.title: Employment category for a child
minor_employment_kind.description: Act 350 s.2(2): light work in a family undertaking; public entertainment licensed by the Director General; work approved by the government for a school or training institution; apprenticeship approved by the Director General. Declare OTHER for work outside these permitted categories.

hazardous_work.title: Fourth Schedule hazardous work
hazardous_work.description: Whether the work falls within Act 350 Fourth Schedule machinery, hazardous environment, construction, timber, offshore or near-water work.

hazardous_work_personal_supervision.title: Personal supervision for hazardous training
hazardous_work_personal_supervision.description: A young person is personally supervised during hazardous work under s.2(1B).

hazardous_work_training.title: Hazardous work under apprenticeship or vocational training
hazardous_work_training.description: A young person is performing hazardous work under an apprenticeship contract or undergoing vocational training (s.2(1B)).

prohibited_minor_employment.title: Fifth Schedule prohibited employment
prohibited_minor_employment.description: Whether work involves prostitution, social escorts/hostesses, alcoholic-beverage production or trade, gambling/lotteries, massage/reflexology, pornography, or prohibited drugs/substances (Act 350 Fifth Schedule).

receiving_pension.description: A certified invalid receiving an invalidity pension: SOCSO charges the employment injury scheme only (Act 4 First Schedule para 12).

disabled.description: A disabled individual registered with JKM: the RM7,000 disabled-individual relief in PCB (Income Tax Act 1967 s.46(1)(e)).

misconduct_dismissal.title: Dismissed for misconduct
misconduct_dismissal.description: Dismissed for misconduct after due inquiry. Statutory consequences apply only where the relevant provision covers the worker; domestic service is excluded from s.14; s.57 and Part XVA have distinct grounds. For covered workers s.60E(3A) also governs untaken annual leave.

pregnant_or_pregnancy_illness.title: Pregnant or ill from the pregnancy at notice (EA s.41A)

statutory.title: Statutory declarations
statutory.description: Employee registrations, exemptions and declared choices captured on this sealed contract.

domestic_servant_notice_given.title: EPF: domestic servant gave notice to be a member
domestic_servant_notice_given.description: EPF standing only. ACT 452 First Schedule paras (2)–(3): a domestic servant is a member only after one month’s notice in the prescribed form to the Board and the employer.

elected_before_1998.title: EPF: elected to contribute before 1 August 1998
elected_before_1998.description: EPF standing only. ACT 452 Third Schedule Part A para 1(c) and Part C para 1(c): a non-citizen who elected to contribute before 1 August 1998 contributes at the Part A rates below 60 and Part C from 60, not Part F.

employee_rate.title: EPF: elected employee rate (Form KWSP 17A (Khas))
employee_rate.description: EPF standing only. A share above the Third Schedule the employee elected; never below it.

registration_number.title: EPF registration number
registration_number.description: The employee's registration/membership number as issued; keep leading zeros.

board_approved_other_scheme.title: EPF: Board approved another provident scheme
board_approved_other_scheme.description: EPF_NON_CITIZEN standing only. ACT 452 First Schedule para (8): a person domiciled outside Malaysia with the Board’s prior written approval to participate in another scheme is not an employee.

first_insured_at_55_or_more.title: SOCSO: first insured at 55 or more
first_insured_at_55_or_more.description: SOCSO standing only. Act 4 First Schedule para 12(i): no contribution was payable for the employee before 55, so the employee is in the Second Category (employment injury only).

registration_number.title: SOCSO registration number
registration_number.description: The employee's registration/membership number as issued; keep leading zeros.

first_insured_at_57_or_more.title: EIS: first insured at 57 or more
first_insured_at_57_or_more.description: EIS standing only. Act 800 First Schedule para 9: no contribution was payable for the employee before 57, so from 57 the employee is outside EIS.

mykas_resident.title: EIS: resident non-citizen with MyKAS or similar card
mykas_resident.description: EIS standing only. Act 800 First Schedule para 10(a)–(c): a foreign employee with a permanent-resident, MyKAS or similar identity card under the National Registration Regulations 1990 is covered.

registration_number.title: EIS registration number
registration_number.description: The employee's registration/membership number as issued; keep leading zeros.

children_disabled_tertiary.title: RM16,000: a disabled child in diploma or degree study
children_disabled_tertiary.description: Income Tax Act 1967 s.48 as declared for MTD (Specification 2026 D, Q × C): the count of qualifying children at this relief amount; a `_half` count is a child whose relief is shared under s.48(4). Family records alone grant no relief.

children_disabled_tertiary_half.title: RM16,000: a disabled child in diploma or degree study — half share
children_disabled_tertiary_half.description: Income Tax Act 1967 s.48 as declared for MTD (Specification 2026 D, Q × C): the count of qualifying children at this relief amount; a `_half` count is a child whose relief is shared under s.48(4). Family records alone grant no relief.

children_tertiary_or_disabled.title: RM8,000: 18 and over in diploma or degree study, or a disabled child
children_tertiary_or_disabled.description: Income Tax Act 1967 s.48 as declared for MTD (Specification 2026 D, Q × C): the count of qualifying children at this relief amount; a `_half` count is a child whose relief is shared under s.48(4). Family records alone grant no relief.

children_tertiary_or_disabled_half.title: RM8,000: 18 and over in diploma or degree study, or a disabled child — half share
children_tertiary_or_disabled_half.description: Income Tax Act 1967 s.48 as declared for MTD (Specification 2026 D, Q × C): the count of qualifying children at this relief amount; a `_half` count is a child whose relief is shared under s.48(4). Family records alone grant no relief.

children_under_18_or_studying.title: RM2,000: under 18, or 18 and over in full-time A-level/matriculation study
children_under_18_or_studying.description: Income Tax Act 1967 s.48 as declared for MTD (Specification 2026 D, Q × C): the count of qualifying children at this relief amount; a `_half` count is a child whose relief is shared under s.48(4). Family records alone grant no relief.

children_under_18_or_studying_half.title: RM2,000: under 18, or 18 and over in full-time A-level/matriculation study — half share
children_under_18_or_studying_half.description: Income Tax Act 1967 s.48 as declared for MTD (Specification 2026 D, Q × C): the count of qualifying children at this relief amount; a `_half` count is a child whose relief is shared under s.48(4). Family records alone grant no relief.

pcb_epf_normal_month.title: PCB: reviewed employee EPF on normal remuneration (K1)
pcb_epf_normal_month.description: Actual/verified expected employee EPF for this month’s normal remuneration, including EPF on tax-exempt cash allowances.0 for an excluded employee. Retain the allocation evidence; the combined contribution remains the statutory scheme’s amount.

socso_eis_relief.title: PCB: claim SOCSO and EIS contributions as TP1 relief
socso_eis_relief.description: Form TP1 2026 item C14 (Income Tax Act 1967 s.46(1)(n); MTD Specification 2026 D.2(ii) item k): the employee claims the SOCSO, EIS and LINDUNG 24 Jam (SKBBK) employee contributions deducted this year as LP1, up to RM350 a year; the relief follows the contributions this payroll actually charged. Payroll never relieves them unclaimed, so the default is false; do not also include them in tp1_monthly_deductions.

tax_residency.title: MTD tax residence
tax_residency.description: Income Tax Act 1967 s.7: residence for the basis year. Unrecorded, a citizen or permanent resident is charged as resident and a FOREIGNER as non-resident at 30% (s.107(2); MTD Specification 2026 D(a)).

tp1_accumulated_deductions.title: PCB: actual prior TP1 deductions this year (ΣLP)
tp1_accumulated_deductions.description: Actual allowable claims from this employment before the declaration month. Enter 0 explicitly if none. Previous-employer amounts belong to tp3_prior_deductions. Respect each deduction category’s remaining annual limit.

tp1_monthly_deductions.title: PCB: TP1 deductions for the month (LP1)
tp1_monthly_deductions.description: Actual allowable TP1 deductions claimed for the stated declaration month (LP1), excluding separately claimed SOCSO/EIS and rebates. Enter actual earlier-year claims in tp1_accumulated_deductions; never multiply this amount by the month number.

tp1_zakat_current.title: PCB: employee-paid TP1 rebate this month
tp1_zakat_current.description: Actual zakat paid directly by the employee, and qualifying departure-levy rebate, claimed through TP1 in tp1_declaration_month. Excludes the ZAKAT payroll deduction and TP3 previous-employer rebate.

tp1_zakat_prior.title: PCB: actual earlier employee-paid TP1 rebates this year
tp1_zakat_prior.description: Actual previous-month TP1 zakat/departure-levy rebates in this employment, excluding payroll ZAKAT deductions and tp3_prior_zakat. Must be updated with tp1_declaration_month.

tp3_prior_deductions.title: PCB: TP3 actual prior allowable deductions

references.title: Employment Act 1955 ss.37–44 and First Schedule para.2(5): Part IX applies to covered female employees and excludes domestic employees. Section 37 grants at least 98 consecutive days per confinement. Allowance eligibility requires at least 90 days in aggregate with the employer during the nine months immediately before confinement and employment with that employer at some time during the four months immediately before confinement (s.37(2)(a)); the surviving-natural-child limit is in ss.37(1)(c)–(d). Service with unrelated employers is not added to qualify against this employer. Sections 37(2)(d)–(3) separately govern multiple-employer claims and contributions. More favourable contractual benefits remain separate. Section 37(2)(b) and Employment (Minimum Rate of Maternity Allowance) Regulations 1976 reg.2 require each eligible calendar day at the greater of ordinary daily pay and RM6. Section 37(2)(c) deems unabated monthly wages to satisfy the allowance; daily/hourly cash targets use s.60I(1C) preceding-period ordinary wages and actual worked days. Official regulations: https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/sites/default/files/2023-03/5.%20EMPLOYMENT%20%28MINIMUM%20RATE%20OF%20MATERNITY%20ALLOWANCE%29%20REGULATIONS%201976_0.pdf Section 37(1)(c) denies allowance where there are five or more surviving children at confinement; s.37(1)(d)(i) limits that count to natural children irrespective of age. The dated natural-child count excludes adopted children, deaths before confinement and births after confinement; same-day death requires a determination of survival at confinement. A CHILD_BIRTH event opens this row for the confinement that bears the allowance (fewer than five surviving natural children, counted from the CHILD_BIRTH and CHILD_DEATH events dated before it, and ninety days employed in the nine months before it) and MATERNITY_LEAVE_NO_ALLOWANCE for the one that does not. 98 days per confinement; births on one date are one confinement.

MATERNITY_LEAVE.description: Paid maternity leave of 98 consecutive days for each confinement (Employment Act 1955 s.37). The maternity allowance needs at least 90 days' employment in the nine months before confinement and fewer than five surviving children.

references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.37(1)(a) and (c)–(d), s.37(2)(a): every covered female employee (not a domestic employee, First Schedule para.2(5)) is entitled to maternity leave of not less than 98 consecutive days per confinement, but no maternity allowance where she has five or more surviving natural children at confinement (counted from the CHILD_BIRTH and CHILD_DEATH events dated before the confinement) or was not employed by the employer for at least 90 days in the nine months before confinement. A CHILD_BIRTH_NO_ALLOWANCE event records an allowance lost otherwise (EA s.40(1)). Those days are leave without pay: MATERNITY_LEAVE carries the paid case. 98 days per confinement; births on one date are one confinement.

MATERNITY_LEAVE_NO_ALLOWANCE.description: Maternity leave of 98 consecutive days without the maternity allowance: for a mother with five or more surviving children, or employed for less than 90 days in the nine months before confinement (Employment Act 1955 s.37). The days are unpaid.

Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations 2010 reg.8(1): a part-time employee’s sick leave is 10 days under two years’ service, 13 from two to under five, 15 from five; none on a non-working day (reg.8(2)). 14 / 18 / 22 days in each calendar year by service (under two years, two to under five, five or more; window CALENDAR_YEAR); part-time 10 / 13 / 15 (Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations 2010 reg.8(1)). references.title: Employment Act 1955 s.60E(1) — 8 days of paid annual leave for less than two years of continuous service, 12 days for two but less than five, and 16 days for five or more. The closing words of s.60E(1) give an employee who has not completed twelve months of continuous service during the year in which the contract terminates an entitlement in direct proportion to the number of COMPLETED MONTHS of service, which is the proration below. EA s.60E(1): a fraction of a day under a half is disregarded and a half or more is a day (`rounding: WHOLE_DAY`). EA s.60E(3A) proviso — no pay-out where the employee is dismissed under s.14(1)(a); `encash_on_exit_when` withholds the exit pay-out on a DISMISSAL recorded as `misconduct_dismissal`. EA s.60E(3B) — leave of absence without pay exceeding thirty days in aggregate in any twelve months is disregarded in computing the length of service "under this section", so all of such leave, not only the days past thirty, comes out of the service the ANNUAL_LEAVE_SERVICE rule counts. Absence without leave is not leave granted and does not come out; s.60F is another section and keeps plain service. Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations 2010 (P.U.(A) 302/2010) reg.7(1): a part-time employee’s annual leave is 6 days under two years’ service, 8 from two to under five, 11 from five — a ladder of its own, not the full-timer’s days prorated by hours. company policy — unused annual leave carries into the next leave year, at most 5 days, expiring at that year’s end, unless the employee’s terms state another number (`terms.annual_leave_carry_limit_days`). EA s.60E(2)–(3) leave carry to the employer and employee’s agreement and set no statutory floor on what carries. EA s.60E(2) lets the leave of each twelve months of service be taken within the twelve months after them, so a year’s unused statutory days — `carry_statutory_bands`, the s.60E(1) and reg.7(1) ladders above, prorated and rounded as the grant is — carry in full, lapsing at the next year’s end; the 5-day cap (or the terms fact) limits only the company’s days above statute. the entitlement is metered per twelve months of continuous service (window SERVICE_YEAR, EA s.60E(1)); the unused days of one service year carry into the next only (EA s.60E(2): leave of each twelve months is taken within the twelve months after them), at most that year's own entitlement, once. a PART_TIME term earns 6 / 8 / 11 days (under two years, two to under five, five or more; Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations 2010 reg.7(1)), prorated by completed months in the first year as s.60E(1) prorates the full-time days. EA s.60E(1), second proviso: an employee absent without permission and without reasonable excuse (days the roster marks ABS in the service year) for more than 10% of the working days of the twelve months (52 weeks × normal days per week, six unrecorded) is not entitled to that year’s paid annual leave. EA s.60E(1) closing words and s.60E(2A) (AGC reprint read 2026-10-08): in the year in which the contract terminates, the leave accrued is in direct proportion to the COMPLETED MONTHS of that service year (the year's band × completed months ÷ 12, a half day or more a day), beside the previous twelve months' leave carried in full; s.60E(3A) pays the untaken days. When the exit is recorded and the day read falls in the exit's service year, the grant is so prorated (completed months to the day after the last day, so a full final year keeps its whole band); the first-year proration already counts completed months.

ANNUAL_LEAVE.description: Paid annual leave per service year: 8 days under two years, 12 from two to under five, 16 from five; part-time 6 / 8 / 11. Paid out at monthly wages ÷ 26 a day (Employment Act 1955 s.60E, s.60I; Part-Time Regulations 2010 reg.7).

references.title: LHDN, Specification for Monthly Tax Deduction (MTD) 2026
references.locator: sections D and E; D(a) note p.9; D(2) Steps 1(C/E) and 4; D(3)-(5); E(9) item v p.21; E(5), E(13), E(15)
references.quote: Resident: year-to-date formula P = Σ(Y − K*) + (Y1 − K1) + (Y2 − K2)n + (Yt − Kt) − (D + S + DU + SU + QC); all EPF relief within RM4,000. D RM9,000 (the only automatic relief, D.2(i) item a); S RM4,000 spouse without income; DU RM7,000 disabled individual; SU a further RM6,000 disabled spouse; QC child relief RM2,000 under 18 or studying, RM8,000 tertiary or disabled, RM16,000 disabled in tertiary education, half amounts for a shared child. Normal MTD = [tax − (Z + X)] ÷ (n + 1), truncated to the sen and rounded up to 5 sen; additional remuneration adds the year’s tax with Yt − Kt; each component under RM10 is not deducted; the month’s zakat is then rebated. Optional deductions item k (D.2(ii)): SOCSO/EIS RM350 a year, the specification’s worked examples carry LP1 = 0 on a RM5,500 wage. D(a): exempt income is excluded from MTD remuneration; "With effect from August 2017, MTD for resident on foreign workers is applicable to employees with an employment contract of or more than 182 days". Non-resident 30%. D(b) and E(13): current additional-remuneration EPF is included once in the additional-pay calculation. D(3)-(5): approved REP, knowledge-worker and relocation C-suite profiles are 15% of projected chargeable income after relief and accumulated PCB/rebates; REP and knowledge-worker profiles retain the RM400/RM800 low-chargeable-income rebate, C-suite none; REP requires Malaysian citizenship, C-suite non-citizenship; REP and C-suite periods are exactly five consecutive assessment years. E(5), E(15): external zakat and religious-travel departure levy are rebates in the accepted claim month; full rebate amounts remain in history even when current PCB is zero. Accumulated MTD excludes CP38 directed instalments; accumulated rebates retain the full qualifying zakat, including TP3 openings. E(9): exempt perquisites leave the MTD remuneration (official travelling allowance up to RM6,000 a year, child care allowance up to RM3,000, awards up to RM2,000 together).

references.title: LHDN, Specification for Monthly Tax Deduction (MTD) 2026
references.locator: sections D and E; D(a) note p.9; D(2) Steps 1(C/E) and 4; D(3)-(5); E(9) item v p.21; E(5), E(13), E(15)
references.quote: Resident: year-to-date formula P = Σ(Y − K*) + (Y1 − K1) + (Y2 − K2)n + (Yt − Kt) − (D + S + DU + SU + QC); all EPF relief within RM4,000. D RM9,000 (the only automatic relief, D.2(i) item a); S RM4,000 spouse without income; DU RM7,000 disabled individual; SU a further RM6,000 disabled spouse; QC child relief RM2,000 under 18 or studying, RM8,000 tertiary or disabled, RM16,000 disabled in tertiary education, half amounts for a shared child. Normal MTD = [tax − (Z + X)] ÷ (n + 1), truncated to the sen and rounded up to 5 sen; additional remuneration adds the year’s tax with Yt − Kt; each component under RM10 is not deducted; the month’s zakat is then rebated. Optional deductions item k (D.2(ii)): SOCSO/EIS RM350 a year, the specification’s worked examples carry LP1 = 0 on a RM5,500 wage. D(a): exempt income is excluded from MTD remuneration; "With effect from August 2017, MTD for resident on foreign workers is applicable to employees with an employment contract of or more than 182 days". Non-resident 30%. D(b) and E(13): current additional-remuneration EPF is included once in the additional-pay calculation. D(3)-(5): approved REP, knowledge-worker and relocation C-suite profiles are 15% of projected chargeable income after relief and accumulated PCB/rebates; REP and knowledge-worker profiles retain the RM400/RM800 low-chargeable-income rebate, C-suite none; REP requires Malaysian citizenship, C-suite non-citizenship; REP and C-suite periods are exactly five consecutive assessment years. E(5), E(15): external zakat and religious-travel departure levy are rebates in the accepted claim month; full rebate amounts remain in history even when current PCB is zero. Accumulated MTD excludes CP38 directed instalments; accumulated rebates retain the full qualifying zakat, including TP3 openings. E(9): exempt perquisites leave the MTD remuneration (official travelling allowance up to RM6,000 a year, child care allowance up to RM3,000, awards up to RM2,000 together).

references.locator: paras 1-2 (normal and additional remuneration): P, K, K1, K2, Kt, n and n + 1; Steps 1-5; Table 1
references.quote: MTD = [(P - M) R + B - (Z + X)] / (n + 1), where P = [sum(Y - K) + (Y1 - K1) + (Y2 - K2) n + (Yt - Kt)] - [D + S + DU + SU + QC + (sum LP + LP1)]. The additional-remuneration method computes the same P with the current month's (Yt - Kt) and withholds the difference between the total tax for the year and X + the normal MTD for the month x (n + 1). Rounding: cut to sen, then up to the next 5 sen; below RM10 no deduction.

references.title: actual year-to-date and a bonus paid once

Y1 is ORDINARY_WAGES less exempt pay, arrears, commission not paid monthly and awards, plus official travel above its limit. Yt is the bonus, arrears, commission not paid monthly, taxable awards and compensation, and final settlements, so one-off pay enters P once; Y2 repeats only Y1. K1 is the declared pcb_epf_normal_month when supplied, otherwise the employee EPF apportioned by EPF wages. In a bonus-only run Y1 is zero, so Y2 is zero and the next normal run catches up through X. references.title: Employees’ Social Security (Amendment) Act 2026 (Act A1788)
references.locator: s.3 (Act 4 s.6(4)-(5), (11)); s.17, Third Schedule column (4)(B) "Non-employment injury"
references.quote: In operation 1 June 2026. First-category contributions by Part I, II or III and second-category by Part IV, V or VI of the Third Schedule for the First, Second and Third Phase; employee share only; the second-category column (4) is the same amount in every band. Introduces the Skim Kemalangan Bukan Bencana Kerja (LINDUNG 24 Jam) under Act 4. Wages to RM200 are the printed amounts; Phase I = round(1.25% × band midpoint, 5 sen, half to even) − 0.5% × midpoint (RM200.01–300 → RM1.85), Phase II = 1.00% × midpoint, Phase III = round(1.25% × midpoint, 5 sen, half to even). Employee share only, 0.75% of wages in Phase 1 (years 1-2 from 1 June 2026), rising to 1.00% in Phase 2 (years 3-5) and 1.25% in Phase 3 (year 6 onwards). Charged in both the First and the Second Category on the same wage bands and the same RM6,000 ceiling as SOCSO. The 65 rows are A1788 Third Schedule Part I column (4)(B) (Part IV column (4) for the Second Category, identical in every band). A six-month grace period from 1 June 2026 runs before penalties. The Second and Third Phase amounts (Parts II/V and III/VI) apply from 1 June 2028 and 1 June 2031. PERKESO’s consolidated Act 4 text (as at 1 September 2022) predates A1724/2024 and A1788 and is not the source of these amounts.
